claims.claim: The laptop FLUS-thermometer number reproduces on Perlmutter (A100, fp32).
claims.value: -2.042 K per 100 W/m² of warming flux [-2.076, -2.012] over 73 states of 1985; wrong sign on 99.85% of open ocean (laptop: −2.04 [−2.08, −2.01], 99.8%)
claims.control: slab law gives +0.33; FLDS/FSNS have the law's sign (0.33 / 0.28)
claims.caveat: 1985 is a TRAINING year; uniform open-ocean shift (a 10×10° box gives ~2×)
claims.command: python -m hc.capture data/states/ic1985 --start 1985 --steps 73 && python phase0/flus_slope.py data/states/ic1985

claims.claim: In E3SM truth, the ocean's FLUS input is a near-exact thermometer of the SST it must predict (a target leak in the data).
claims.value: conditional slope -17.0 K per 100 W/m² of warming flux (literal 1/(4εσT³): −17.3); thermometer sign on 99.5% of open ocean; per-cell R² median 0.9983 (2045–49)
claims.control: the other four fluxes have conditional slopes ≈ 0 (medians |·| < 0.003)
claims.caveat: per-cell OLS with intercept; the preregistered alignment check (end vs start of window, pooled RMS) does NOT show the 20% margin (22.21 vs 22.28 W/m²) because a spatial offset dominates pooled RMS

claims.claim: C1A0 does not copy the truth thermometer: it uses about a tenth of it, with an unrelated spatial pattern, and keeps lawful-sign responses to the other fluxes.
claims.value: model/truth slope ratio 0.109; pattern correlation +0.03 (-0.02 without ice-shelf cavities); model FLUS -1.84 vs truth -16.93 K per 100 W/m² (2045 states vs 2045–49 truth)
claims.verdict: preregistered verdict: something else to explain
claims.control: same result on 1995 states (ratio 0.109, r = 0.07); FLDS/FSNS model slopes +0.32/+0.29 vs truth ≈ 0
claims.caveat: model states are coupled-run inputs from truth ICs (not truth-forced); uniform shifts only for this comparison

claims.claim: Below “skip.0 + layer 0”: FLUS splits about evenly between layer 0's linear 1×1 skip_module and its InstanceNorm-ed convblock, whereas an SST perturbation goes 100% through the 1×1 skip_module.
claims.value: FLUS uniform: skip.0 0.86, skip_module 0.53, convblock 0.47; box: skip.0 0.91, skip_module 0.35, convblock 0.65; sst: skip_module 1.00
claims.verdict: 2045 (score year), 19 states, exact patching; 1995 replicates to ±0.01
claims.control: projection metric agrees within 0.05 for FLUS. Skeptic pass: an independent implementation (exege's new samudra Patchable adapter, EdgePatch semantics) gives skip.0 share 0.854 on 7 states of 2045 (localize.py: 0.86)
claims.caveat: near-linear response: sufficiency = necessity, shares sum to ≈1 (one result per split)
claims.command: python idea1_flus/localize.py data/states/t2045 t2045 4 && python idea1_flus/localize_summary.py t2045

claims.claim: InstanceNorm statistics account for the box-vs-uniform difference of the FLUS response.
claims.value: freezing the convblock's IN statistics raises its uniform-shift share 0.47 → 0.94 (box: 0.65 → 0.65); predicted un-normalised uniform slope -2.65 vs measured box -2.58 K per 100 W/m² (uniform -1.80)
claims.control: the same freeze leaves box shares unchanged, as expected if a box barely moves whole-field statistics
claims.caveat: holds for FLUS only: for FLDS the same prediction gives 1.34× vs measured box/uniform 1.07×; box ratio here is 1.43× (laptop said ~2×)

claims.claim: At layer-0 channel granularity the FLUS shortcut cannot be removed without breaking FLDS; at the input it can.
claims.value: greedy-32 channels (selected on fit states 1985 + 1995, scored on 2045): FLUS ×0.08 but FLDS ×-0.06; replacing the FLUS input with 5.67e-8·sst⁴ keeps FLDS/FSNS ×1.00/×1.02 and shifts the clean next SST by +0.17 K (open-ocean mean; RMS 0.49 K)
claims.verdict: PREREG rule: channel sets fail; input replacement passes (FLUS = 0 by construction)
claims.control: 20 random size-matched sets per size: FLUS ×0.97 (10) / ×0.87 (32) median, 0 successes
claims.caveat: mean ablation at one place (layer-0 output); box shifts move SHFLX by +67% under input replacement; the one-step +0.17 K is what the coupled de-leak tests over years
claims.command: python idea1_flus/ablate.py l0 data/states/ic1985,data/states/t1995 data/states/t2045 v1 && python idea1_flus/ablate_summary.py ablate_l0_v1

claims.claim: Every ocean checkpoint has the FLUS thermometer; its strength tracks how leaky the FLUS it was last trained on was.
claims.value: ocean-only E11 seeds -4.23…-3.99; after more ocean-only fine-tuning (E11-FT) -7.07…-6.85; after coupled fine-tuning (C1A0, C1A1, C0A0, E30/E31 seeds) -2.49…-1.71 K per 100 W/m² (uniform, 1995 truth-forced inputs)
claims.verdict: 17/17 have the shortcut (thermometer sign > 75% of area)
claims.control: truth's conditional slope is −17: every model is far below it; in this sample, coupled fine-tuning also turns LHFLX from the wrong sign to the lawful one
claims.caveat: C1A1 shares C1A0's ocean init and E11-FT S01 is C1A0's ocean before coupled fine-tuning (not independent); E17 (1-day ocean) excluded: 5-day inputs

claims.claim: With balanced perturbations, C1A0 keeps the amount of each scale about as E3SM does, but decorrelates the pattern faster, increasingly so at small scales.
claims.value: U_7 projection vs truth AR(1): l≈8 0.83 vs 0.98; l≈31 0.52 vs 0.73; l≈55 0.27 vs 0.45; magnitude at l≈55 0.43
claims.control: truth per-degree AR(1) on fit and score years (agree within 0.02); preregistered single-variable probes shown for contrast
claims.caveat: probe = one 5-day truth difference direction per state (12 states × 3 noise draws); truth AR(1) averages all anomalies; T_1 is the exception (small scales persist more than in truth); l ≤ 2 includes global means
